items.name: hoverlab
items.title: Hoverlab
items.description: The Hoverlab design system: light and dark CSS variables, radius scale and icon library. Install this first and every Hoverlab block and page inherits it.

items.name: preset-hoverlab
items.title: Hoverlab — a Hoverlab preset
items.description: What this site wears — a green brand over faintly warm neutrals, 12px corners, standard gutters. The catalog as it ships. Start here if you like how the blocks look on this site.

items.name: preset-console
items.title: Console — a Hoverlab preset
items.description: Almost no chroma anywhere, square corners, tighter gutters and slightly smaller type. Developer tools and anything data-heavy, where colour should mean something rather than decorate.

items.name: preset-studio
items.title: Studio — a Hoverlab preset
items.description: A warm brand over warm neutrals with large corners and generous spacing. Marketing sites and consumer products — the shape that reads as calm rather than capable.

items.name: preset-cockpit
items.title: Cockpit — a Hoverlab preset
items.description: Cool violet accent, small corners, tight gutters, smaller type throughout. Dashboards and admin panels that have to show a lot at once without shouting.

items.name: preset-signal
items.title: Signal — a Hoverlab preset
items.description: High-chroma amber on lightly tinted neutrals, at the catalog’s own proportions. Consumer apps and launches — the one that looks least like a developer tool.

items.name: kit-saas-launch
items.title: SaaS launch kit
items.description: Marketing site, auth, dashboard and billing — the whole first release. One install writes 25 of its 26 pieces; the template is a separate scaffold.

items.name: kit-ai-product
items.title: AI product kit
items.description: Thread, reasoning trace, approvals, citations — and the meter that bills them. One install writes 22 of its 23 pieces; the template is a separate scaffold.

items.name: kit-storefront
items.title: Storefront kit
items.description: Browse, filter, buy, pay, and the receipt afterwards. One install writes 25 of its 26 pieces; the template is a separate scaffold.

items.name: kit-internal-tools
items.title: Internal tools kit
items.description: Tables that sort, filter, bulk-edit and page — plus the shell around them. One install writes 22 of its 23 pieces; the template is a separate scaffold.

items.name: kit-waitlist
items.title: Waitlist kit
items.description: One page, one form, one evening. One install writes 13 of its 14 pieces; the template is a separate scaffold.

items.name: kit-content-and-docs
items.title: Content and docs kit
items.description: A blog, a documentation site, a changelog and a careers page. One install writes 19 of its 21 pieces; the templates are a separate scaffold.

items.name: path-landing-page
items.title: Build a landing page
items.description: Eight blocks, in the order that converts. One install writes all 8 blocks.

items.name: path-waitlist
items.title: Launch a waitlist page
items.description: One screen, one field, live in an evening. One install writes all 6 blocks.

items.name: path-auth-flow
items.title: Ship a complete auth flow
items.description: Every screen a real sign-in needs, including the ones people forget. One install writes all 6 blocks.

items.name: path-onboarding
items.title: Onboard a new user
items.description: The first ten minutes, from sign-up to first real action. One install writes all 6 blocks.

items.name: path-states
items.title: Handle the states nobody designs
items.description: Loading, empty, error, missing — the four screens that decide whether it feels finished. One install writes all 6 blocks.

items.name: path-settings
items.title: Build a settings area
items.description: Five screens, in the order people go looking for them. One install writes all 5 blocks.

items.name: path-product-updates
items.title: Publish what you shipped
items.description: A changelog, a roadmap, and a way to hear about both. One install writes all 5 blocks.

items.name: path-dashboard
items.title: Build an internal dashboard
items.description: The shell, the numbers, and the table underneath. One install writes all 7 blocks.

items.name: path-billing
items.title: Add billing and usage
items.description: From the price on the marketing page to the invoice in the account. One install writes all 5 blocks.

items.name: path-storefront
items.title: Build a storefront
items.description: Browse, choose, buy — the whole commerce path. One install writes all 8 blocks.

items.name: path-ai-assistant
items.title: Build an AI assistant
items.description: From the blank thread to an action the user actually approved. One install writes all 10 blocks.

items.name: hero-split
items.title: Split Hero with Product Panel
items.description: Copy on the left, a drawn product panel on the right — the default hero for anything with an interface to show, with no image asset to host and no layout shift while it loads.

items.name: hero-centered
items.title: Centered Announcement Hero
items.description: A linked announcement pill over a large centered headline, dual CTAs and a wordmark strip — the hero for a product with nothing to screenshot yet.

items.name: hero-screenshot
items.title: Hero with Browser Frame
items.description: Centered copy above a screenshot in window chrome, masked at the bottom so a tall image never dictates the height of the fold. Wraps your own img or video.

items.name: hero-waitlist
items.title: Waitlist Hero with Email Capture
items.description: A pre-launch hero whose only ask is an email address, with pending and success states and a signup count that argues for finishing rather than starting.

items.name: hero-search
items.title: Search-First Hero
items.description: A hero whose primary action is a real search form with prefilling suggestion chips — for marketplaces and directories, where sending the visitor below the fold to find the search box is the whole failure.

items.name: hero-terminal
items.title: Developer Hero with Install Command
items.description: A drawn terminal whose install line is real, selectable text with a working copy button and a feature-detected clipboard call — the hero for anything adopted by typing rather than signing up.

items.name: hero-app-download
items.title: App Download Hero with Phone
items.description: A drawn phone beside two store links built as real anchors rather than badge images, so they inherit the theme, need no hosted asset and carry an accessible name that is not a filename.

items.name: hero-testimonial
items.title: Hero Anchored by a Customer Quote
items.description: Pitch on the left, a marked-up figure and blockquote on the right, so the claim and the evidence for it share the fold instead of sitting a scroll apart.

items.name: hero-metrics
items.title: Hero with Proof Metrics
items.description: A centered hero closing on a definition list of scale numbers, with a masked grid wash behind it — for infrastructure and payments, where "how many" is the second question a buyer asks.

items.name: hero-editorial
items.title: Editorial Masthead Hero
items.description: A serif display headline over a 60-character standfirst and a real byline, with one text link and no competing CTAs — the hero for publications and essays, where the writing is the product.

items.name: hero-media-overlay
items.title: Full-Bleed Media Hero
items.description: Copy over your own image or video, with a graded scrim and deliberately fixed light-on-dark text — because the background is a photograph in both themes, so flipping the copy would break it.

items.name: hero-integrations
items.title: Integration Wall Hero
items.description: A hero whose visual is the connector list itself, marked up as a real list so a visitor can skim it for their own stack — asset-free initials tiles, no third-party marks to license.

items.name: hero-booking
items.title: Appointment Booking Hero
items.description: A day strip built as a radio group rather than buttons, so arrow keys move between dates and sold-out days disable properly — the fold for anything sold by the appointment.

items.name: hero-price-anchor
items.title: Hero with Inline Price
items.description: Names the price above the fold for single-plan and one-time products, with the former price in a real strikethrough element so it is never announced as the current one.

items.name: navbar-simple
items.title: Responsive Navbar
items.description: Brand, links and CTAs with a mobile panel that unmounts when closed — so its links are never tabbable while invisible — plus escape-to-close and focus return.

items.name: announcement-bar
items.title: Dismissible Announcement Bar
items.description: The strip above the navbar, with the three things it usually gets wrong fixed: a named region, a live role only when it earns one, and a dismissal that persists.

items.name: navbar-mega-menu
items.title: Navbar with Mega Menu
items.description: Top-level items that open a described-link panel, opening on hover and focus, closing on escape, outside click and focus leaving the group — and collapsing to an accordion on mobile.

items.name: nav-mobile-drawer
items.title: Mobile Nav Drawer
items.description: A slide-in site menu that behaves like a dialog: focus trap, focus restoration, body scroll lock and a transition that drops under prefers-reduced-motion.

items.name: navbar-authenticated
items.title: Signed-in Application Bar
items.description: The bar above an app rather than a site: workspace and environment named in the open, a bell that counts in words, and an impersonation strip that cannot be dismissed.

items.name: footer-mega
items.title: Mega Footer with Link Columns
items.description: Brand column, four labelled nav columns, socials and a legal bar — the one place every page links to every section. Ships no client JavaScript.

items.name: footer-minimal
items.title: Minimal Footer Bar
items.description: One row — brand, a handful of links, socials, copyright — for a site where a five-column footer would be whitespace pretending to be structure.

items.name: footer-newsletter
items.title: Footer with Newsletter Band
items.description: A raised email-capture band overlapping a three-column link footer, with the confirmation replacing the field in place rather than navigating away.

items.name: footer-status-locale
items.title: App Footer with Status
items.description: The footer of a signed-in product rather than a marketing site: a live status line with words as well as colour, plus locale and theme as native selects.

items.name: footer-compliance
items.title: Regulated Seller Footer
items.description: Legal entity, company number, registered address, VAT and the consumer links an EU or UK seller has to publish — with a region control that changes the terms, not just the currency.

items.name: contact-form-split
items.title: Split Contact Form
items.description: A contact form beside the channels that bypass it — a real address, a support link and a response-time promise, which is what makes a form people cannot see into feel worth filling.

items.name: multi-step-form
items.title: Multi-Step Form with Validation
items.description: A three-step form where each step validates only its own fields, errors are wired to inputs with aria-describedby, and advancing moves focus to the new heading.

items.name: booking-scheduler
items.title: Meeting Scheduler
items.description: Day strip, slot grid and a time zone the visitor can change — because a slot list with no zone on it is how this pattern wastes an hour of everyone involved.

items.name: feedback-widget
items.title: Inline Feedback Widget
items.description: One click to rate, everything after it optional — the shape that collects a complaint from someone mid-task who would never open a contact page.

items.name: form-error-summary
items.title: Form with Error Summary
items.description: The state every form reaches and none of them illustrate: a focused summary at the top linking to each bad field, validation that waits for submit, and somewhere for the failure that belongs to no field.

items.name: contact-sales-form
items.title: Contact Sales Form
items.description: A qualifying contact form that asks the three things a first reply needs, and says what happens next before you send it.

items.name: support-ticket-form
items.title: Support Ticket Form
items.description: A support form that asks for the one thing that halves resolution time — what you already tried — and says when a human will read it.

items.name: confirm-dialog
items.title: Destructive Confirm Dialog
items.description: A type-to-confirm dialog built on native <dialog>, so the focus trap, top layer and escape handling come from the browser. Focus lands on Cancel, and the button says the verb.

items.name: cookie-consent
items.title: Cookie Consent Banner
items.description: Per-category consent where refusing is exactly as easy as accepting, nothing non-essential is pre-ticked, and the page behind it stays readable — the shape the law expects, wired to your own script gating.

items.name: slide-over-panel
items.title: Slide-Over Edit Panel
items.description: A side sheet for editing a record without losing the list behind it — native <dialog> for the trapping, a data attribute for the slide, and a sticky footer so Save never scrolls away.

items.name: filter-drawer-facets
items.title: Faceted Filter Drawer
items.description: Facets with per-option counts, zero-result options disabled rather than hidden so the list never jumps, and a pending selection applied on a button that says how many choices changed.

items.name: share-access-dialog
items.title: Share & Access Dialog
items.description: The share modal where a design mistake is a data leak: general access stated as its consequence rather than its setting, and a copy button that never silently widens access.

items.name: bottom-sheet-mobile
items.title: Mobile Bottom Sheet
items.description: Half and full snap points where the content owns the scroll and overscroll-contain keeps the page behind still. The drag handle is a real button, Escape and the backdrop close it, and safe-area padding keeps the last row pressable.

items.name: modal-unsaved-changes
items.title: Unsaved Changes Prompt
items.description: The interception that keeps work: three answers rather than two, the changed fields listed by name, a destructive-styled discard, and Escape resolving to cancel.

items.name: drawer-record-detail
items.title: Record Inspector Drawer
items.description: A non-modal drawer that keeps the list on screen, with previous and next controls for moving between records and an activity tab beside the fields.

items.name: onboarding-checklist
items.title: Setup Checklist with Progress
items.description: The get-started card that ships with its first item already ticked, a native <progress> element rather than a div bar, and a dismiss control that appears only once there is nothing left to abandon.

items.name: setup-wizard
items.title: Guided Setup Wizard
items.description: A choice-driven wizard with a persistent side rail, real radio groups in a fieldset so arrow keys work, and visited steps navigable while steps ahead stay out of the tab order.

items.name: team-invite-step
items.title: Team Invite Step
items.description: The onboarding step where a product becomes multiplayer: pasted addresses split into chips, typos marked rather than dropped, and an honest way to skip.

items.name: product-tour-coachmark
items.title: Product Tour Coach Mark
items.description: A tour step anchored to the control it explains, with a spotlight cut by one spread shadow, a visible step count and focus that follows the step.

items.name: onboarding-role-picker
items.title: Role Picker
items.description: The "what best describes you" step, asked honestly — every option states what it actually changes, the skip is visible and names what you get instead, and the choice is reversible.

items.name: onboarding-import-data
items.title: Import or Start Empty
items.description: The empty product’s real first question. Sample data is offered with equal weight rather than as grey small print, every connector names its scope before the redirect, and each option carries the honest duration.

items.name: workspace-setup-form
items.title: Workspace Setup Form
items.description: The first screen after signup, asking only the two things that cannot be changed silently later.

items.name: data-migration-split
items.title: Data Migration Split
items.description: What a migration actually moves and what it cannot, stated before the switch rather than discovered after it.

items.name: toast-stack
items.title: Toast Notification Stack
items.description: A corner stack whose live region is mounted before any message exists, errors announce assertively, and the auto-dismiss timer pauses on hover and on focus.

items.name: notification-inbox
items.title: Notification Inbox Panel
items.description: The bell panel: filterable list with read state, the unread count in the accessible name rather than only in a badge, and machine-readable timestamps beside the human ones.

items.name: notification-preferences
items.title: Notification Preferences Matrix
items.description: Per-event, per-channel switches as a real table, with required notifications locked and explained, and column headers that toggle a whole channel and report a mixed state honestly.

items.name: push-permission-prompt
items.title: Push Permission Pre-Prompt
items.description: The soft ask before the browser dialog you only get one shot at — what will be sent, what will not, and a decline of the same weight as the yes.

items.name: notification-digest-list
items.title: Notification Digest
items.description: A day's notifications collapsed into one digest, grouped by what they are rather than when they arrived.

items.name: digest-schedule-form
items.title: Digest Schedule Form
items.description: The control that turns notification volume down instead of off, which is the choice most people actually want.

items.name: notification-channel-list
items.title: Notification Channel List
items.description: Which channel carries which event, so the loud ones can be moved rather than muted entirely.

items.name: stats-band
items.title: Hairline Stats Band
items.description: A four-up metrics strip with 1px hairline dividers, built from a single gap-px grid so the rules stay crisp on any display.

items.name: stats-cards
items.title: Stat Cards with Deltas
items.description: Metrics carrying the direction they moved, with the good direction declared per stat so a falling churn rate reads as a win — arrow and text, never colour alone.

items.name: stats-narrative
items.title: Stats Beside the Argument
items.description: Four figures in a hairline card next to the paragraph making the claim, each carrying an optional source line — for numbers that mean nothing without knowing lower than what, over how long, across how many.

items.name: stats-comparison
items.title: Before-and-After Metric Table
items.description: The buyer’s current situation in one column and yours in the next, as a real table with scoped headers — the comparison they are actually making, which a delta against your own past cannot express.

items.name: stats-timeline
items.title: Milestone Timeline
items.description: The same measurement taken year after year down a vertical rail, each with the event that explains it — the shape for trajectory, which no snapshot of four numbers can claim.

items.name: stats-benchmark-band
items.title: Benchmark Stat Band
items.description: Performance figures with the measurement method printed beside each one, so a sceptical reader can check rather than take them.

items.name: security-posture-band
items.title: Security Posture Band
items.description: The compliance and security facts a procurement reviewer asks for, stated as figures with their scope rather than as badges.

items.name: logo-cloud
items.title: Seamless Logo Marquee
items.description: An infinite horizontal logo scroll with masked edges, a pause-on-hover affordance and a reduced-motion fallback that wraps instead of moving.

items.name: logo-grid
items.title: Bordered Logo Grid
items.description: Hairline-separated cells that hold still and show the whole set at once — the logo wall for a footer, a customers page, or anywhere the count is the claim.

items.name: logo-strip
items.title: Under-Hero Logo Strip
items.description: One unbordered line of wordmarks beside a claim you can actually be wrong about, sized to sit under a hero without pushing the CTA down or moving while the headline is being read.

items.name: logo-segments
items.title: Logos Grouped by Industry
items.description: Customer logos under segment headings as a description list, with an “and 40 more” count for the ones under NDA — answers whether you have done this for someone like the reader, which a flat wall cannot.

items.name: bento-features
items.title: Bento Feature Grid
items.description: Six tiles on an asymmetric 4x3 grid with per-tile spans, a hover glow and a mobile collapse that follows source order.

items.name: feature-rows
items.title: Alternating Feature Rows
items.description: A full row per feature with the media side flipping each time, so the eye re-enters the page instead of skimming a stack of identical blocks.

items.name: feature-icon-grid
items.title: Icon Feature Grid
items.description: Uniform cells, no spans, no state — the grid for nine things that matter equally, where a bento would be a wall and tabs would be a filing cabinet.

items.name: integration-grid
items.title: Integration Directory Grid
items.description: What each integration actually does, not a wall of logos — with availability as a text pill rather than a tinted border, and the name as the link so the card is not one enormous one.

items.name: persona-cards
items.title: Audience Persona Cards
items.description: A "who this is for" grid: four cards naming an audience, the outcome they want and the bullets that get them there.

items.name: code-showcase
items.title: Editor Window Showcase
items.description: A feature section paired with a tabbed fake editor — real selectable code, generated line numbers and a copy button.

items.name: feature-tabs
items.title: Tabbed Feature Showcase
items.description: Features as a real tablist — arrow keys, roving focus and a drawn product panel per tab — for the section where four features would otherwise fight for one scroll.

items.name: integration-depth-split
items.title: Integration Depth Split
items.description: An integrations section that says how deep each one goes, instead of a wall of logos that all imply the same thing.

items.name: pricing-tiers
items.title: Three-Plan Pricing Toggle
items.description: Three plans with a monthly/yearly switch, yearly prices derived from the monthly figure so the two can never disagree.

items.name: pricing-single
items.title: Single-Plan Price Card
items.description: One price given a whole card, with the objection a one-time price raises answered under the button rather than in a FAQ further down.

items.name: pricing-usage-calculator
items.title: Tiered Usage Calculator
items.description: A slider that turns a rate card into the number a buyer actually cares about, with a per-tier breakdown so the total can be checked rather than taken on trust.

items.name: comparison-table
items.title: Plan Comparison Matrix
items.description: A real table with scoped headers, a sticky first column and screen-reader text behind every check and dash.

items.name: pricing-credits
items.title: Prepaid Credit Packs
items.description: One-time packs with the per-credit price worked out for the reader and the saving stated rather than implied — the pricing shape for a product that sells quantity, not a subscription.

items.name: pricing-plan-picker
items.title: In-App Plan Picker
items.description: A native radiogroup of plans with the current one disabled and the prorated charge announced as it changes — the upgrade dialog, not the marketing table.

items.name: pricing-value-split
items.title: Pricing Value Split
items.description: The case for the price, made beside the price — what the alternative costs, in the units a buyer already measures.

items.name: plan-limits-list
items.title: Plan Limits List
items.description: What actually runs out on each plan, including what happens when it does — the row a pricing table leaves off.

items.name: testimonial-grid
items.title: Masonry Testimonial Wall
items.description: Quotes packed by height using CSS multi-column, with star ratings, initial avatars and no ragged bottom edge.

items.name: testimonial-spotlight
items.title: Single-Quote Spotlight
items.description: One customer, quoted at length and backed by a stat row — the section for when a single believable story argues better than a wall of five-star fragments.

items.name: testimonial-ratings
items.title: Aggregate Rating Breakdown
items.description: A mean score over a stated sample with all five rating bands left visible, including the one-star row — proof that survives the objection every hand-picked quote wall invites.

items.name: testimonial-carousel
items.title: Scroll-Snap Quote Rail
items.description: Twenty quotes in the height of six, scrolled by CSS snap points with arrows that disable at the ends — no auto-advance, and every quote stays in the DOM for search and Cmd-F.

items.name: testimonial-video
items.title: Video Testimonial Cards
items.description: Poster tiles linking out to recordings, each with a pull-quote that has to land for the majority who never press play, and a drawn placeholder until you supply a still.

items.name: customer-outcome-band
items.title: Customer Outcome Band
items.description: Testimonials reduced to the measured outcome and the conditions it happened under, for readers who skip the quotes.

items.name: faq-accordion
items.title: No-JS FAQ Accordion
items.description: Exclusive accordion behaviour from named <details> elements — no state, no hooks, no JavaScript, full keyboard support for free.

items.name: faq-two-column
items.title: Two-Column FAQ with Help Rail
items.description: Questions on the right against a sticky rail that keeps a route to a human in view — for the visitor whose objection is not on the list.

items.name: faq-grid
items.title: Open FAQ Grid
items.description: Every answer rendered and visible in a two-column description list — the FAQ shape for a marketing page, where collapsed text is text a search engine will not quote.

items.name: faq-categorized
items.title: FAQ Grouped by Topic
items.description: Anchor-linked topic pills over per-topic details groups with the first answer open — for the FAQ that outgrew a single list, working with JavaScript disabled.

items.name: faq-search
items.title: Filterable FAQ with Fallback
items.description: A search that narrows the list across answers and keywords, announces the count, and turns an empty result into the contact route it should always have been.

items.name: faq-objection-list
items.title: Objection FAQ
items.description: An FAQ written from the objections that stop a sale rather than from the questions that are comfortable to answer.

items.name: security-faq-list
items.title: Security FAQ
items.description: The security questions a buyer's IT reviewer asks, answered with scope and dates rather than with the word "enterprise-grade".

items.name: changelog-timeline
items.title: Release Timeline
items.description: A dated changelog on a vertical rail with added/changed/fixed tags and machine-readable <time> values.

items.name: roadmap-columns
items.title: Public Roadmap Columns
items.description: Shipped / in progress / planned in three columns, with status carried by icon as well as colour.

items.name: blog-post-grid
items.title: Blog Index Grid
items.description: A featured post at full width above a card grid, with drawn covers built from tokens — a blog index with no image pipeline and no broken-thumbnail state.

items.name: article-header
items.title: Article Header & Byline
items.description: Kicker, headline, standfirst, byline and share row, with the opening prose and a pull quote included — the type scale of a post, decided once instead of per-article.

items.name: team-grid
items.title: Team Grid
items.description: An about-page team section on initials avatars rather than photos, so shipping it never waits on headshots and there is no broken-image state to design.

items.name: job-listing-board
items.title: Careers Openings Board
items.description: Openings grouped by department with location, type and salary on every row — candidates self-select by craft first, and a flat list makes them scan for it.

items.name: docs-layout
items.title: Three-Column Docs Frame
items.description: Sidebar, article and on-this-page rail — each column answers a different question, and they collapse on mobile in the order that keeps the article alive.

items.name: api-endpoint-card
items.title: API Endpoint Reference
items.description: Method badge, path, parameter table and a request/response pair kept side by side — an example request whose response is a scroll away gets pasted blind.

items.name: code-tabs-panel
items.title: Package Manager Code Tabs
items.description: One install command behind npm/pnpm/yarn/bun tabs with a working copy button — every reader uses exactly one package manager, so showing all four wastes three lines.

items.name: newsletter-signup
items.title: Newsletter Capture Band
items.description: Email capture with a four-state submission machine and an aria-live status line, so the outcome is announced and not just shown.

items.name: community-band
items.title: Community Link Band
items.description: A closing CTA of three link cards pointing at GitHub, chat and social — somewhere to go for the visitor who is not ready to convert.

items.name: cta-split-panel
items.title: Closing CTA Panel
items.description: A rounded gradient panel that restates the offer for the reader who scrolled past everything — heading left, both CTAs right, reassurance points underneath.

items.name: cta-sticky-bar
items.title: Sticky Conversion Bar
items.description: The call to action that follows a long page down — held back until the reader is past a scroll threshold, dismissible, and spaced so it never covers the content it is selling.

items.name: cta-inline-card
items.title: In-article CTA Card
items.description: The offer that sits inside the column instead of interrupting it — a labelled aside a screen reader can skip in one keystroke, tied to the paragraph above it, with the friction admitted before the click.

items.name: referral-waitlist-form
items.title: Referral Waitlist Form
items.description: A waitlist capture that shows position and referral credit, turning a dead-end confirmation into the one action that moves the queue.

items.name: demo-request-form
items.title: Demo Request Form
items.description: A demo request that offers the self-serve escape first, so the people who did not want a call do not book one.

items.name: auth-login-card
items.title: Email & Social Login Card
items.description: Centred sign-in card with social providers, a password reveal toggle and the autoComplete values password managers actually need.

items.name: auth-signup-split
items.title: Split Signup With Proof
items.description: Registration form beside a testimonial panel, with live password rules and a proof column that drops rather than stacks on mobile.

items.name: auth-otp-verify
items.title: One-Time Code Input
items.description: Six-box OTP entry that handles paste, backspace, arrow keys and iOS SMS autofill — the parts hand-rolled versions always miss.

items.name: auth-forgot-password
items.title: Password Reset Request
items.description: Reset-link request with a sent state worded to avoid leaking whether an account exists.

items.name: auth-reset-password
items.title: New Password With Strength Meter
items.description: Set-a-new-password form with a four-step strength meter, confirm matching and errors announced rather than only coloured.

items.name: auth-two-factor
items.title: Two-Factor Challenge
items.description: Authenticator-code prompt with a backup-code escape hatch and an opt-in trusted-device checkbox that is off by default.

items.name: auth-sso-domain
items.title: Email-First SSO Sign-In
items.description: Email first, then whatever that domain uses. The password field is absent rather than disabled when SSO is enforced, the button names the company it redirects to, and a personal address is a normal answer instead of an error.

items.name: auth-magic-link-form
items.title: Magic Link Sign In
items.description: Passwordless sign-in that says what will land in the inbox and how long it lasts, before the address is typed.

items.name: sso-enterprise-split
items.title: Enterprise SSO Split
items.description: What SSO actually covers, written for the person who has to configure it rather than the person who asked for it.

items.name: dashboard-shell
items.title: Sidebar Dashboard Shell
items.description: Sidebar, top bar and scrollable content slot, with a mobile drawer that closes on Escape and marks the active route.

items.name: dashboard-stat-cards
items.title: KPI Cards With Deltas
items.description: Metric row where each card knows whether a rise is good news, so churn going up is red while revenue going up is green.

items.name: dashboard-activity-feed
items.title: Activity Feed Panel
items.description: Recent-events list with typed icons and relative timestamps that keep the absolute value in a <time> element.

items.name: dashboard-page-header
items.title: Page Header With Tabs
items.description: Breadcrumb, title, action buttons and a counted tab row that sits flush with the bottom rule.

items.name: kanban-board
items.title: Kanban Board Columns
items.description: Four columns of prioritised, tagged, assigned task cards with a blocked state — the board as a layout contract, leaving drag behaviour to your own state and library.

items.name: activity-timeline
items.title: Audit Log Timeline
items.description: Events grouped by day on a vertical rail, icons varying by type and one entry expanded into a detail card — what keeps forty events scannable instead of forty gray dots.

items.name: calendar-month
items.title: Month Calendar Grid
items.description: A month view where event chips truncate and overflow becomes "+n more", so a busy Tuesday never changes the height of the row it sits in.

items.name: dashboard-saved-views
items.title: Saved View Tabs
items.description: Saved views with the third state most implementations drop: a shared view with unsaved edits, where Save changes what a colleague sees tomorrow. Two honest buttons instead of one, ownership on the tab, and dirty said in words.

items.name: dashboard-comparison-period
items.title: Comparison Period Picker
items.description: A reporting window with the comparison window spelled out beside it — resolved dates, UTC arithmetic, and an option to align weekdays so a weekend is never compared against a Tuesday.

items.name: dashboard-alert-rules
items.title: Alert Rule List
items.description: Threshold alerts with the two facts most rule lists omit: how often each has fired, and whether its channel is muted — so a rule that is on but delivering nowhere reads as its own state.

items.name: data-table-sortable
items.title: Sortable Selectable Table
items.description: Type-aware sorting with aria-sort, a header checkbox that goes properly indeterminate, and selection that survives a re-sort.

items.name: data-table-toolbar
items.title: Table Search & Filter Bar
items.description: Search, filter count and view switch, with active filters shown as removable chips so a filtered table never looks unfiltered.

items.name: data-table-pagination
items.title: Pagination With Page Window
items.description: Page size, range summary and a fixed-width number window that stays the same size from page 1 to page 200.

items.name: data-table-expandable
items.title: Expandable Detail Rows
items.description: Rows that open into a full-width detail panel via colSpan, with aria-expanded and aria-controls wired to the detail row.

items.name: data-table-column-manager
items.title: Column Show, Hide & Reorder
items.description: Reordering that works from the keyboard rather than by drag alone, pinned columns that cannot be hidden or moved, and a guard so the last visible column cannot be unchecked into a blank table.

items.name: data-table-bulk-actions
items.title: Bulk Action Bar
items.description: The selection bar that asks the question most tables skip: this page, or all 1,284 rows the filter matches. Typed confirmation above a threshold, an undo with the window counting down, and a select-all that names its own scope.

items.name: data-table-inline-edit
items.title: Inline Editable Table
items.description: Edit cells in the grid with staged changes, per-cell validation, the original value kept beside the attempt, and a save that counts what is still pending.

items.name: data-table-grouped-rows
items.title: Grouped Table with Subtotals
items.description: Collapsible group headers that carry their own subtotals while collapsed, with a grand total that sums every row rather than only the visible ones.

items.name: crud-create-form
items.title: Create Record Form
items.description: A full-page create form with a guidance rail and a Save-and-create-another that keeps the shared fields - the shape a record with more than six fields actually needs.

items.name: crud-create-modal
items.title: Create Record Modal
items.description: Three fields over the list they add to, with the new row appearing behind the dialog rather than after it closes.

items.name: crud-create-drawer
items.title: Create Record Drawer
items.description: A long create form in a side drawer: the fields scroll, the header and the action bar do not, and the list stays legible beside it.

items.name: crud-read-page
items.title: Record Detail Page
items.description: The read view arranged by what a reader came for - a verdict band of four facts, then details, then the related records a field dump can never show.

items.name: crud-read-modal
items.title: Record Quick Look
items.description: The verification modal from a table row: copyable identifiers, no editing, nothing scrolling, and the row still marked behind it.

items.name: crud-update-form
items.title: Edit Record Form
items.description: An edit page that shows the diff - per-field change markers carrying the previous value, a per-field revert, and a Save button that counts what it will write.

items.name: crud-update-modal
items.title: Edit Record Modal
items.description: The edit modal including the parts nobody draws: the in-flight state, the rejected save that keeps your typing, and the conflict when someone else got there first.

items.name: crud-update-drawer
items.title: Field-Level Edit Drawer
items.description: The save-on-blur model, with per-field confirmation, per-field failure and a written-in-this-session log - the only honest answer to what did I just change.

items.name: crud-delete-cascade
items.title: Cascade Delete Dialog
items.description: Deleting a record other records depend on: dependents counted and grouped by fate - deleted, orphaned, retained - with a guard that scales to the blast radius.

items.name: crud-success-state
items.title: Record Created State
items.description: The screen after the write: the reference copyable, next actions ranked rather than listed, and an undo window that counts down honestly and then says why it is gone.

items.name: crud-bulk-edit-drawer
items.title: Bulk Edit Drawer
items.description: One change applied to many records that disagree - mixed values shown as mixed, untouched fields never written, and skipped rows counted before you commit.

items.name: crud-archive-restore
items.title: Archive and Restore
items.description: The bin with the clock on it: days until purge per row, who archived it, and a restore disabled with a reason when the parent has already gone.

items.name: settings-nav-layout
items.title: Grouped Settings Layout
items.description: Sidebar-and-panel settings shell that becomes a horizontal scroller on mobile instead of collapsing into a select.

items.name: settings-profile-form
items.title: Profile Form With Save Bar
items.description: Avatar, fields and a character counter, with a sticky save bar that only appears once something has genuinely changed.

items.name: settings-team-members
items.title: Team Members & Invites
items.description: Member list with role selects, pending invites shown inline, and the last owner locked so a workspace cannot be orphaned.

items.name: settings-api-keys
items.title: API Key Management
items.description: Masked keys, a create flow that reveals the secret exactly once, and a revoke that confirms before it fires.

items.name: settings-danger-zone
items.title: Danger Zone
items.description: Destructive actions gated by typing the resource name exactly — the pattern GitHub and Stripe use, and for good reason.

items.name: settings-sessions
items.title: Active Sessions & Devices
items.description: The screen people go looking for after losing a laptop. Sign out everywhere states what it does not reach — API keys keep working — locations are written as estimates, and this device is labelled rather than revocable by misclick.

items.name: settings-notification-matrix
items.title: Notification Channel Matrix
items.description: Every event against every delivery channel in one grid, with column toggles and required rows that show the policy instead of a disabled checkbox.

items.name: settings-audit-log
items.title: Audit Log
items.description: A compliance-grade trail with named actors, before and after values, IP addresses, and a stated retention window — plus a count of what the active filter is hiding.

items.name: empty-state-cta
items.title: Empty State With Illustration
items.description: Two variants — nothing created yet, versus filters excluded everything — because offering "create your first" to a bad filter is the classic bug.

items.name: error-state-retry
items.title: Error State With Retry
items.description: Failed-to-load panel with a visible retry, a copyable error reference and the stack tucked behind a disclosure.

items.name: not-found-404
items.title: 404 With Search & Suggestions
items.description: A 404 that helps: a real GET search form that works without JavaScript, likely destinations, and home as the fallback rather than the headline.

items.name: skeleton-list
items.title: Shimmer Skeleton List
items.description: Loading placeholders with varied row widths and a sweep that is motion-safe only, falling back to a flat tint under reduced motion.

items.name: permission-denied-state
items.title: Permission Denied (403)
items.description: The state where the page exists and the account is not on the list: names who can grant access, sends the request, and leaks nothing about what is inside.

items.name: offline-state-banner
items.title: Offline With Queued Changes
items.description: Leads with what still works — three edits saved on this device — instead of with the failure. The retry backoff counts down in the open, and the three things that genuinely cannot work offline are named rather than discovered.

items.name: empty-filtered-results
items.title: Empty Because of Filters
items.description: The empty state for a list emptied by its own filters: every active filter shown as a removable chip ordered by how many results it would restore, with clear-all deliberately second.

items.name: maintenance-window-state
items.title: Scheduled Maintenance Window
items.description: Planned downtime with a live countdown, an end time in the reader’s timezone, what still works — and a different sentence once the window overruns rather than a negative timer.

items.name: metric-sparkline-cards
items.title: Sparkline Metric Cards
items.description: KPI cards with a hand-built SVG trend line — no charting dependency for a path this file computes in twelve lines.

items.name: bar-chart-panel
items.title: CSS Bar Chart Panel
items.description: Categorical bars in plain CSS with gridlines, hover values and a screen-reader table carrying the real numbers.

items.name: usage-meter-panel
items.title: Quota & Usage Meters
items.description: Consumption against plan limits, with warning thresholds, honest overage display and unmetered quotas that do not fake a bar.

items.name: line-chart-panel
items.title: Dual-Series Line Chart
items.description: A year-over-year trend in inline SVG with a printed axis, no charting dependency and the same data repeated as a screen-reader table.

items.name: donut-breakdown
items.title: Donut Breakdown
items.description: Where a total went, drawn as one conic-gradient ring with the total in the hole and every number repeated in the legend.

items.name: activity-heatmap
items.title: Daily Activity Heatmap
items.description: A year of daily activity as one square per day, bucketed against a quantile so a single outlier cannot flatten the scale.

items.name: funnel-conversion-panel
items.title: Conversion Funnel
items.description: A funnel that leads with the step-to-step rate and the people who fell out of it, not the tidy share-of-top percentages nobody can act on. Biggest drop named in words, and a footnote saying which definition of funnel this is.

items.name: metric-alert-list
items.title: Metric Alert List
items.description: Alert thresholds with their current distance from firing, so a quiet alert is visibly armed rather than possibly broken.

items.name: kpi-summary-band
items.title: KPI Summary Band
items.description: The top-of-dashboard figures, each carrying the comparison period that makes a delta mean anything.

items.name: billing-plan-summary
items.title: Plan & Next Charge Summary
items.description: Current plan, next charge with an actual figure and date, payment method, and a prominent pending-cancellation state.

items.name: invoice-history-table
items.title: Invoice History
items.description: Past invoices with tabular figures, worded statuses rather than bare coloured dots, and per-invoice download labels.

items.name: payment-method-card
items.title: Payment Methods On File
items.description: Cards on file with the two failures that cost the subscription: expiry called out before it fails, and the default stated on the row rather than implied by ordering.

items.name: subscription-cancel-flow
items.title: Subscription Cancel Flow
items.description: Self-serve cancellation with no dark patterns: the exact date access ends, what breaks, one honest alternative, and a button that works.

items.name: usage-overage-notice
items.title: Overage Notice with Projection
items.description: Past the included allowance, with the end-of-month projection and every number the invoice will use — because a surprise bill is a product defect.

items.name: billing-seat-manager
items.title: Seat Count & Proration
items.description: Changing seats with the bill shown first: the part-period charge and the new recurring amount as two numbers, the arithmetic spelled out, and the asymmetry stated where it bites — removing a seat refunds nothing today.

items.name: billing-invoice-detail
items.title: Invoice Detail
items.description: One invoice with the arithmetic shown: proration split into a credit and a charge with their own date ranges, tax as a line with its jurisdiction, and totals in a real tfoot.

items.name: billing-credit-balance
items.title: Credit Balance and Expiry
items.description: Consumable credits split into the buckets they actually live in, rendered in spend order, with a proportional warning that only appears when a meaningful balance is about to expire.

items.name: support-chat-widget
items.title: Support Chat Widget
items.description: The corner launcher, with real availability instead of a stock reassurance, article deflection before the form, no self-opening, and a way to make it go away.

items.name: message-bubble-thread
items.title: Message Bubble Thread
items.description: Bubbles with the parts that get skipped: per-message delivery state, grouping by author and time, day separators, and a retry on the failed bubble itself.

items.name: message-attachment-bubble
items.title: Attachment Bubbles
items.description: Five kinds of thing that is not text - image, document, link, location and an upload still in flight - each answering the question its own kind raises.

items.name: inbox-thread-list
items.title: Inbox Thread List
items.description: The list half of a two-pane inbox, with unread and selected as visibly different states and bulk selection as a mode rather than a hover checkbox.

items.name: inbox-thread-detail
items.title: Inbox Reading Pane
items.description: The reading pane with the composer always present, quoted history collapsed behind a count, and an internal-note mode whose send button names the recipient.

items.name: voice-message-player
items.title: Voice Message Player
items.description: A voice note you can navigate: a waveform that is a real seek control, a speed button, a transcript, and a played state that survives finishing.

items.name: video-call-layout
items.title: Video Call Layout
items.description: The call grid with the state that makes it usable - active speaker, per-tile connection quality, hide self-view, and the you-are-muted nudge.

items.name: call-device-settings
items.title: Call Device Settings
items.description: The green room, where every picker has a test beside it - an input meter, a test tone, a camera preview - and blocked permission is a state, not an error.

items.name: support-ticket-thread
items.title: Support Ticket Thread
items.description: The customer side of a ticket, where a named owner and a deadline replace Status: Open - including the waiting-on-you state that stops the argument about response times.

items.name: command-palette
items.title: Command Palette
items.description: The ⌘K switcher done properly: focus stays in the input while aria-activedescendant moves, arrows wrap, and the highlight resets on every query change.

items.name: search-results-panel
items.title: Grouped Search Results
items.description: Results grouped by section with visible breadcrumb paths and <mark>-highlighted matches — users recognise where a result lives faster than they read its snippet.

items.name: keyboard-shortcuts-sheet
items.title: Keyboard Shortcuts Sheet
items.description: The "?" overlay, with chords written once in one notation and rendered per platform — mod becomes Command on Apple and Ctrl everywhere else, decided after mount so the markup never mismatches.

items.name: applied-filters-bar
items.title: Applied Filters Bar
items.description: The strip above a result set that answers "why am I only seeing four things" — every active constraint as a removable chip, with the excluded count beside it.

items.name: search-autocomplete
items.title: Header Search with Suggestions
items.description: The field in the header, not the palette over it: Enter searches for what you typed unless you arrowed to a suggestion, late responses are dropped by sequence number, and recent searches are removable one at a time.

items.name: search-facet-panel
items.title: Faceted Refinement Panel
items.description: Faceted search with result counts on every option, zero-count options kept visible and disabled so the list stays stable, and a note explaining why the counts do not sum.

items.name: search-scope-switcher
items.title: Search Scope Switcher
items.description: One query counted across every scope it could have matched, as a real tablist with arrow-key movement — so an answer that is nowhere is visible without opening four tabs.

items.name: recent-search-list
items.title: Recent Search List
items.description: The empty state of a search box, filled with the searches that are worth repeating and the ones worth saving.

items.name: search-faceted-results
items.title: Faceted Search Results
items.description: The whole faceted search assembled - rail, chips, live count and sort - with the intersection actually applied and relevance offered only when there is a query.

items.name: search-facet-range
items.title: Range Facet with Histogram
items.description: The facet that is a number: a distribution over a dual-thumb slider built from two real range inputs, with typed bounds clamped on blur rather than per keystroke.

items.name: file-dropzone
items.title: Drag & Drop Upload
items.description: Dropzone with per-file progress and a drag counter that fixes the flicker every naive dragleave handler produces.

items.name: upload-progress-list
items.title: Upload Progress List
items.description: The list that follows the dropzone: complete, uploading, queued and failed rows with cancel and retry — because hiding the failure is the classic upload bug.

items.name: upload-resumable
items.title: Resumable Large Upload
items.description: One big file on a connection that will drop: a bar allowed to go backwards when a chunk is retried, a time estimate that is a range or nothing, and a promise about closing the tab made before it is needed.

items.name: csv-import-mapper
items.title: CSV Column Mapper
items.description: The screen between "file uploaded" and "data imported": source columns mapped to schema fields, with a sample value under each and required fields blocking the button.

items.name: avatar-crop-upload
items.title: Avatar Crop & Upload
items.description: Framing a profile photo with keyboard-operable zoom and position, showing what gets trimmed rather than hiding it behind the mask.

items.name: upload-requirements-form
items.title: Upload Requirements Form
items.description: An upload form that states the constraints before the file is chosen, rather than rejecting it after a two-minute transfer.

items.name: import-from-url-form
items.title: Import From URL Form
items.description: The import path for a file that is already on the internet, which does not need to travel through the browser at all.

items.name: chat-thread-panel
items.title: Assistant Thread with Composer
items.description: A scrolling conversation with per-turn actions, announced as a polite log restricted to additions — so a streaming reply is not re-read on every token — and auto-scroll that only pins when the user is already at the bottom.

items.name: chat-prompt-bar
items.title: Composer with @ Sources and / Commands
items.description: The trigger menus done properly: @ and / open only at a token boundary, the query is derived from the caret so the menu closes itself, and focus never leaves the textarea — the combobox pattern, not a floating div.

items.name: chat-streaming-answer
items.title: Streaming Answer with Citations
items.description: Token-by-token text with linked citations, follow-up chips and a caret that stops the moment the stream does. The status is announced once; the prose is deliberately outside every live region.

items.name: chat-empty-state
items.title: Assistant Starter Screen
items.description: The blank thread, answered: grouped starter prompts as real lists of buttons, each group labelled, so the highest-leverage screen in an AI product is not a centred logo.

items.name: chat-message-branches
items.title: Message Version Switcher
items.description: The answers a regenerate throws away — siblings rather than replacements, an edited question that branches in place, and a plain sentence about what happens to the replies below.

items.name: chat-artifact-canvas
items.title: Chat Beside a Canvas
items.description: The two-pane assistant layout, with the mismatch nobody else states: the canvas names the version it is showing and says so when that is not the one the conversation is about. Versions link back to the turn that made them.

items.name: chat-model-picker
items.title: Model Picker with Trade-offs
items.description: Model selection with the three numbers the choice actually turns on — capability, latency and cost per message — and locked models explained rather than greyed out.

items.name: chat-attachment-tray
items.title: Prompt Attachment Tray
items.description: Files staged against a prompt with a running context-token budget, unreadable files flagged before send, removal allowed mid-upload, and a send button that names its one blocker.

items.name: agent-thinking-trace
items.title: Collapsible Thinking Trace
items.description: The "thought for 5s" panel: a native details/summary outside, individually expandable steps inside — buttons rather than nested disclosures, which are announced as a disclosure within a disclosure.

items.name: agent-tool-calls
items.title: Tool Call Chips
items.description: Dense tool invocations that open into their arguments and result, with status carried by icon and word rather than colour, and errors marked as alerts only once the user opens them.

items.name: agent-task-list
items.title: Live Agent Task List
items.description: Run status as rows — done, running, failed, queued — with native progress elements, per-task retry buttons that name their task, and progress announced from one small status region instead of every row.

items.name: agent-working-indicator
items.title: Working Indicator with Elapsed Time
items.description: The gap before the first token: a shimmer grid, a phase label that advances as the wait lengthens, and a running counter — which is the only honest answer to "is it stuck". The timer is hidden from the live region on purpose.

items.name: agent-run-failure
items.title: Failed Run Trace
items.description: The trace after something broke: retries counted in the open with what each one cost, a step that was silently worked around drawn in amber rather than green, and the raw error kept apart from the agent’s reading of it.

items.name: agent-retry-log
items.title: Agent Retry Log
items.description: What the agent tried, what failed, and what it did about it — the run history a user needs before they trust a second attempt.

items.name: agent-cost-breakdown
items.title: Agent Cost Breakdown
items.description: What one run cost, per step, so an expensive answer is attributable rather than a monthly surprise.

items.name: approval-request-card
items.title: Approval Request with Blast Radius
items.description: The agent stops and asks: the effect stated before the verb, choices as radios in a fieldset so picking is separate from committing, no pre-focused Approve, and the decision left on screen afterwards.

items.name: agent-diff-review
items.title: Proposed Edits Diff Table
items.description: Machine-proposed row edits accepted one at a time, with before and after in real del/ins elements, a tri-state select-all that actually sets indeterminate, and a running count of what will be written.

items.name: confidence-recommendation
items.title: Recommendation with Confidence Meter
items.description: A suggestion scored with a native meter rather than a styled bar, banded in words as well as numbers, and showing what the model rejected — the fastest way a human catches a bad recommendation.

items.name: permission-scope-dialog
items.title: Agent Permission Scopes
items.description: Read and write scopes separated rather than bundled, writes off by default, a required expiry, and switches that are real checkboxes with role="switch" — so the grant is toggleable by keyboard and announced as on or off.

items.name: approval-queue
items.title: Bulk Approval Queue
items.description: Forty decisions and an honest way to clear them: bulk approve that cannot reach the high-impact rows, a select-all that says how many it takes, and the auto-approve deadline on every line.

items.name: approval-policy-list
items.title: Approval Policy List
items.description: Which agent actions run unattended and which need a signature, stated as a policy the operator can read before anything happens.

items.name: escalation-queue-list
items.title: Escalation Queue
items.description: What is waiting on a person, ordered by how long it has been waiting rather than when it arrived.

items.name: human-oversight-split
items.title: Human Oversight Split
items.description: Where a person sits in an automated run, written as four guarantees rather than as a promise that a human is involved.

items.name: context-chunk-cards
items.title: Retrieved Context Chunks
items.description: The RAG debugging surface: ranked passages with similarity as a meter, matched spans in real mark elements, and filter chips wired as a radiogroup so arrows move between them.

items.name: source-citation-list
items.title: Answer Source Citations
items.description: The published footnotes under an answer — ordered list, real cite and time elements, the claim each source supports, and a staleness warning written in words rather than shown as an amber dot.

items.name: knowledge-source-picker
items.title: Knowledge Source Picker
items.description: Choosing what the assistant may read, with indexing state told honestly — a half-indexed source says so rather than showing a green tick — and the footer stating the effect of the selection, not its cardinality.

items.name: retrieval-empty-state
items.title: Nothing Found, Answered Honestly
items.description: The refusal screen: says plainly that nothing was found, shows where it looked and the near-misses below threshold, and offers the two real ways out instead of inventing an answer.

items.name: context-window-budget
items.title: Context Window Budget
items.description: What is in the context and what fell out of it — a stacked budget with the reply reserve drawn as a segment, and the dropped chunks named with the reason, which is the part nobody ships.

items.name: retrieval-index-status
items.title: Index Freshness Panel
items.description: A green tick means the connector works, not that the answers are current. Freshness as an age in words per source, the headline taken from the stalest one, and a failed sync that still says what age it is answering from.

items.name: retrieval-freshness-list
items.title: Retrieval Freshness List
items.description: Retrieved sources ranked by how stale they are, because a confident answer from a two-year-old document is the failure people do not catch.

items.name: context-scope-list
items.title: Context Scope List
items.description: Which sources this answer may draw on, shown as a scope the user can read before asking rather than a citation list after.

items.name: grounding-split
items.title: Grounding Split
items.description: How an answer is tied to its sources, and what the system does when it cannot find any.

items.name: selection-ai-toolbar
items.title: Selection Action Toolbar
items.description: Highlight a passage and hand it to the model. Positioned from the range rect relative to its container, raised by selectionchange so Shift-Arrow works, and every button prevents the mousedown that would collapse the selection.

items.name: ai-inline-suggestion
items.title: Ghost Text Completion
items.description: Copilot-style completion in a plain textarea: a transparent-caret field over a metric-matched mirror, Tab to accept, Escape that actually sticks, and the suggestion announced rather than left as invisible grey text.

items.name: ai-inspector-panel
items.title: Agent-Adjusted Inspector
items.description: The model edits real properties and every change is attributed and reversible — per-property provenance in words, per-property revert, and sliders whose aria-valuetext carries the unit.

items.name: ai-insight-cards
items.title: Unprompted Insight Cards
items.description: Findings the agent surfaced on its own, paged one at a time, each stating its magnitude rather than its direction, dismissible, and carrying a sparkline that is also a sentence for anyone who cannot see it.

items.name: ai-slash-menu
items.title: Editor Slash Menu
items.description: The "/" menu inside a document: focus never leaves the editor, every row names what it acts on, and Escape cleans up the trigger text it inserted instead of leaving you to backspace it.

items.name: ai-action-menu
items.title: Inline AI Action Menu
items.description: The actions offered on a selection, each saying whether it rewrites in place or opens a draft beside it.

items.name: product-grid
items.title: Product Card Grid
items.description: Responsive product cards with sale badges, ratings and a wishlist button layered above the card link so it stays clickable.

items.name: product-filter-sidebar
items.title: Faceted Filter Sidebar
items.description: Category, size, colour and price facets as proper fieldsets, with colour swatches that carry their name as well as their hue.

items.name: collection-toolbar
items.title: Collection Sort Toolbar
items.description: Result count, sort and density switch — with the count in an aria-live region, since it is the only feedback a filter change gives some users.

items.name: product-rail
items.title: Scroll-Snap Product Rail
items.description: A "you might also like" row on native scroll-snap — touch swiping, momentum and keyboard support for free, with no carousel library.

items.name: product-compare-table
items.title: Product Comparison Table
items.description: Three products side by side with the row labels pinned through a horizontal scroll, an "only show differences" toggle that says how many rows it hid, and "best" marked only where better means something.

items.name: stock-availability-list
items.title: Stock Availability List
items.description: Availability per variant stated before the cart, because discovering it at checkout is where the basket gets abandoned.

items.name: collection-story-split
items.title: Collection Story Split
items.description: The editorial header above a collection grid, carrying the four facts that decide a considered purchase.

items.name: product-gallery
items.title: Product Image Gallery
items.description: Main image with a thumbnail strip built as a real tablist, so arrow keys work and the ratio is fixed to stop the buy box shifting.

items.name: product-buy-box
items.title: Variant & Add-to-Cart Box
items.description: Price, variant radiogroup, quantity stepper and add-to-bag — with sold-out sizes disabled and visible rather than hidden.

items.name: product-info-accordion
items.title: Product Details Accordion
items.description: Description, materials, delivery and returns in named <details> elements — no JavaScript, and the copy stays indexable while collapsed.

items.name: product-review-summary
items.title: Rating Distribution Summary
items.description: Average rating with a clickable histogram — because a 4.3 of forties and fives is a different product from a 4.3 of ones and fives.

items.name: product-size-guide
items.title: Size Guide
items.description: The panel that decides whether the parcel comes back: what the model is wearing and what previous buyers did, above a table whose inches are converted rather than maintained twice.

items.name: product-spec-split
items.title: Product Spec Split
items.description: The specification table beside the product image, with the two or three figures that decide the purchase pulled out of it.

items.name: back-in-stock-form
items.title: Back In Stock Form
items.description: The capture that replaces a dead sold-out button, with the honest caveat that a notification is not a reservation.

items.name: cart-drawer
items.title: Slide-Over Cart Drawer
items.description: A basket panel with the dialog mechanics usually missing: focus trap, focus return, Escape to close and a background scroll lock.

items.name: cart-line-items
items.title: Editable Cart Lines
items.description: Quantity steppers and remove-with-undo, with every total derived rather than stored so the basket can never disagree with itself.

items.name: checkout-form
items.title: Checkout Address & Payment
items.description: The full autocomplete token set that lets a browser fill eight fields in one tap, plus address labels that follow the selected country.

items.name: order-summary-panel
items.title: Order Summary With Promo
items.description: Subtotal, discount, delivery and tax all derived from the lines, with the free-delivery nudge driven by the same threshold as the charge.

items.name: checkout-express-payment
items.title: Express Payment Row
items.description: The wallet buttons above the form, and what they do to it: the address a wallet returns is shown and stays editable, and the row disappears entirely when no wallet is actually available.

items.name: gift-options-form
items.title: Gift Options Form
items.description: The gifting step, placed in the cart where it is a choice rather than at checkout where it is friction.

items.name: gift-card-purchase
items.title: Gift Card Purchase
items.description: The only checkout where the buyer is not the recipient - live preview, a send date with a stated timezone, and the confirm-the-address field that prevents the expensive typo.

items.name: guest-checkout-form
items.title: Guest Checkout
items.description: Guest as the default and the whole form, with a real autocomplete token on every field and the account offer moved to the end, where it costs one checkbox.

items.name: discount-modal
items.title: Discount Offer Modal
items.description: The offer popup with four rules applied: triggered by intent, a decline button of equal weight, a dismissal that is remembered, and the terms on its face.

items.name: order-confirmation
items.title: Order Confirmation
items.description: The thank-you screen built to prevent two support emails: a selectable order number and a delivery date range rather than "soon".

items.name: order-history-list
items.title: Order History
items.description: Past orders with stacked item thumbnails and worded statuses — people recognise what they bought long before the order number.

items.name: review-list
items.title: Customer Reviews
items.description: Sortable reviews with verified-purchase badges, optimistic helpful votes and a real expand control instead of a fade that hides text.

items.name: order-tracking-timeline
items.title: Order Tracking Timeline
items.description: The fortnight between buying and reviewing, answered properly: an arrival range rather than a date, exceptions above the timeline, and a copyable carrier reference.

items.name: review-submit-form
items.title: Write a Review
items.description: The form that produces the reviews the other blocks display — a real radio group for stars, and a prompt that changes with the rating because one star and five need different questions.

items.name: order-lookup-form
items.title: Order Lookup Form
items.description: Order tracking for the guest who never made an account, which is most of them.

items.name: review-distribution-band
items.title: Review Distribution Band
items.description: The rating summary with the numbers that make an average trustworthy — the count, the spread and the verified share.

items.name: warranty-coverage-panel
items.title: Warranty Coverage Panel
items.description: A verdict for this serial number today, with exclusions given equal weight to cover and an extension offered only while it can still be bought.

items.name: refund-request-form
items.title: Refund Request Form
items.description: Refunds are per line, not per order: a reason on each line that drives what is asked for next, and a running total itemising the restocking fee and the delivery rule.

items.name: refund-status-tracker
items.title: Refund Status Tracker
items.description: Where the money is and who is holding it - four stages, each naming the responsible party, including the bank stage every where-is-my-refund contact comes from.

items.name: refunds-overview-table
items.title: Refunds Overview Table
items.description: The operator queue, sorted oldest-open-first because recency is the wrong default, with blocked as a first-class status that names its blocker.

items.name: return-exchange-picker
items.title: Return or Exchange Picker
items.description: Refund, exchange or credit decided per line, with live stock on the variants and the price difference shown before the goods are posted rather than after.

items.name: return-label-instructions
items.title: Return Label and Instructions
items.description: The screen between approved and posted: three drop-off methods with the thing that actually blocks each one, the packing rules that get returns refused, and a date rather than a duration.

items.name: repair-request-form
items.title: Service Repair Request
items.description: A repair is not a return - a symptom picker that filters the service routes, warranty resolved inside the form, and an estimate with its uncertainty stated.

items.name: review-history-list
items.title: Review History
items.description: The reviews you wrote and the ones you owe, with editing that is honest about being marked as edited and moderation that names the rule it applied.

items.name: gift-card-balance
items.title: Gift Card Balance Check
items.description: A balance checker built for the two ways it goes wrong - an empty card and an expired one - answering with a transaction history rather than a bare zero.

items.name: saas-landing-page
items.title: SaaS Landing Page
items.description: A complete marketing page in the order that actually converts — hook, proof, substance, price, objections, exit. Twelve blocks, navbar and footer included.

items.name: pricing-page
items.title: Pricing Page
items.description: Plans, a feature matrix and a pricing-specific FAQ written to remove the last purchase objection rather than answer general questions.

items.name: waitlist-landing-page
items.title: Waitlist Landing Page
items.description: A pre-launch page for a product you cannot buy yet: one email field, scarcity instead of adoption, and no pricing section to be held to later.

items.name: developer-tool-landing-page
items.title: Developer Tool Landing Page
items.description: Install command first, real code before any prose, and a usage calculator instead of tiers — the order a developer actually scans in.

items.name: mobile-app-landing-page
items.title: Mobile App Landing Page
items.description: Store badges above the fold, the App Store rating as the first proof, and a single price — a page with one job, which is the install.

items.name: agency-landing-page
items.title: Agency Landing Page
items.description: A studio site: full-bleed hero, client list, engagements described as engagements, and the actual team — with no pricing, on purpose.

items.name: local-service-landing-page
items.title: Local Service Landing Page
items.description: A booking widget above the fold, every price published including the awkward ones, and a footer carrying the registrations a regulated trade must show.

items.name: marketplace-landing-page
items.title: Marketplace Landing Page
items.description: Two audiences, one page: a search field and real listings for buyers up top, the seller economics below, and a searchable FAQ because they ask different things.

items.name: enterprise-landing-page
items.title: Enterprise Landing Page
items.description: Built for a champion assembling an internal case: numbers in the hero, a comparison that concedes two rows, video references, and published prices instead of a sales wall.

items.name: integration-platform-landing-page
items.title: Integration Platform Landing Page
items.description: The connector names in the hero, a catalogue with honest live/beta/planned status, four SDK languages, credit pricing, and a dated roadmap for everyone who is not on the list.

items.name: creator-course-landing-page
items.title: Creator Course Landing Page
items.description: One person selling one course: a student testimonial as the hero because a course cannot demo, a long instructor section, one price and a refund policy on the page.

items.name: blog-index-page
items.title: Blog Index
items.description: The post grid, a subscribe ask that comes after the proof, and a minimal footer — no hero, because the featured post already is one.

items.name: article-page
items.title: Article Page
items.description: A single post: header, byline and opening prose in one reading column, with the subscribe form after the article — at the only moment it converts.

items.name: careers-page
items.title: Careers Page
items.description: Team first, openings second, then the questions candidates only ask after an offer — answered while they can still change who applies.

items.name: docs-page
items.title: Documentation Page
items.description: The site navbar over the three-column docs frame. In your project this is one catch-all route — the slug picks the article, the frame never changes.

items.name: help-centre-page
items.title: Help Centre
items.description: Search first, the six answers that absorb the most contact volume under it, and the ticket form in plain sight rather than behind a modal — a support page measured in tickets not filed.

items.name: changelog-page
items.title: Changelog Page
items.description: The release timeline with the site chrome kept on, and the one subscribe form on the site that is not a detour — "tell me when this page changes" is exactly what it promises.

items.name: dashboard-overview
items.title: Dashboard Overview
items.description: The screen an app opens on: shell, header, KPI row, chart and activity feed — numbers first, shape second, changes last.

items.name: ai-assistant-page
items.title: AI Assistant Screen
items.description: An agent working inside a real app: a transcript down the middle — reasoning, answer, then the one card that can act — with what it may read and what it noticed demoted to a rail.

items.name: project-board-page
items.title: Project Board
items.description: A kanban board inside the app shell, with tabs that admit the board is one view among several and a header whose primary action is creating work.

items.name: customers-table-page
items.title: Customer List Screen
items.description: The canonical CRUD list — header, toolbar, sortable table and pagination framed as one panel instead of three stacked cards.

items.name: settings-account-page
items.title: Account Settings
items.description: Profile, team, API keys and danger zone in one screen — with the destructive panel last, well away from the everyday controls.

items.name: billing-page
items.title: Billing & Usage Screen
items.description: Plan, quota meters and invoice history, with the upgrade prompt placed beside a bar that is nearly full rather than on the plan card.

items.name: login-page
items.title: Sign-In Screen
items.description: A full auth page that deliberately contains almost nothing but the form — no nav, no marketing, nothing competing with the one job.

items.name: error-404-page
items.title: 404 Page
items.description: Drops straight into app/not-found.tsx, and keeps the site header and footer — on a 404 the navigation is the most useful thing on screen.

items.name: collection-page
items.title: Product Collection
items.description: Sticky filter sidebar, sort toolbar and product grid — with the facets dropped rather than stacked on mobile, so a shopping page does not open as a form.

items.name: product-detail-page
items.title: Product Detail
items.description: Gallery, sticky buy box, details accordion and reviews — ordered by what a shopper needs before they can decide.

items.name: cart-page
items.title: Shopping Bag
items.description: Editable lines beside a sticky summary, so the total and the checkout button survive a scroll through four quantity changes.

items.name: checkout-page
items.title: Checkout
